talk: Dockhand: 'Check your seals twice. I will check them a third time, for a fee.'
Clerk: 'Manifests go in triplicate. The third copy is for the Lane. The Lane never reads it.'
A mother counts crates aloud. She has counted them four times. The number is still the same.
Dockhand: 'Buy your rations here. Out there they cost more and taste worse.'
Overheard: 'My brother went in spring. No word yet. That's the Lane for you: quiet.'
Mattie's boy sweeps the floor. He says Mattie is never wrong, only early.
Clerk: 'Flare season opens September fifteenth. Plan your last three legs accordingly.'
Old Belter at the rail: 'Never outrun a flare. Hide behind something big and be bored.'
A man sells lucky bolts, three credits each. They are ordinary bolts. They sell well.
Dockhand: 'Spare drive parts are cheaper here. You will want two. Everyone wants two, later.'
A child asks if Proxima b has trees. Her father says it has 'prospects'.
Lane clerk: 'Sign here to confirm you were warned. We warn everybody. It is very fair.'
Postmaster: 'Letters home are free. Replies are your problem.'
Dockhand: 'Everything here is red. Don't ask about the paint. It was not paint.'
Chandler: 'Fresh ration stock came in Tuesday. By fresh I mean Tuesday.'
Overheard: 'The Ring was easy. Wait until the Shoals dream about you.'
Clerk: 'Line forms at the left. The left is shorter. The left is also closed.'
A colonist writes his twelfth letter home. All twelve say 'fine'.
Dockhand: 'Ceres is 250 Mk of nothing. Buy extra rations for the nothing.'
Lane clerk: 'Relay staff are on break. I am a volunteer. The break is mine too.'
Trader: 'Prices are up. So is everyone's opinion of the prices.'
A kid peers out the viewport. 'Is that Mars?' 'It's a rock with ambitions,' says her aunt.
Mechanic: 'Your drive sounds like a goat. A healthy goat. Mostly.'
Overheard: 'Tug captains up here quote by the klick. Haggle. They respect it.'
Depot hand: 'Welcome to Ceres. We have rations, parts and quite a lot of rock.'
Clerk: 'The Belt Crossing is dense this year. Hire a tug or hire a prayer.'
Belter in the canteen: 'Never thread a gap you can't see the end of. I did. Hence the arm.'
Chandler: 'Drone charges, boxes of twenty. Scan wrecks, find rations, avoid heroics.'
Overheard: 'Jupiter's Eye is worth the look. It is not a detour. It is the route.'
Dockhand: 'We roll the rocks in on Fridays. Please don't be here on Fridays.'
A widow sells hydroponic tomatoes. Her sign says: 'Grown with love and mild neglect.'
Depot clerk: 'Pilot wait at the Belt is four days. Pilot opinions are free.'
Mechanic: 'Gyros don't fail. They retire. Usually without notice.'
A boy sorts bolts by size and mood. He is paid per bolt.
Overheard: 'My cousin hired a Belter pilot. Lost nothing but his pride. And two crates.'
Lane clerk: 'Please report all drift incidents. Drifting is discouraged.'
Dockhand: 'Ice moon, warm welcome. The welcome is the only warm thing.'
Clerk: 'Saturn Ring Plane is next. Thin ring, fat rocks. Hire a tug if you value your paint.'
Overheard: 'Don't drink the water. I mean, drink it. Just not the first glass.'
Priest: 'Bless your ship? Ten credits. Bless your recycler? Fifteen. It needs it more.'
Trader: 'Everything is priced for people who have already left Earth.'
Dockhand: 'The ice cracks at night. It's not you. It's the ice.'
A miner winks: 'Frozen sea down there. Fish, maybe. Nobody has proved otherwise.'
Lane clerk: 'Spares, rations, suits. We do not sell optimism. Out of stock.'
Mechanic: 'Take a spare of everything. Take two of the thing you think you won't need.'
Overheard: 'After the Rings, Titan. After Titan, the Gate. Eat well before the Gate.'
A boy asks what Proxima smells like. His mother says: 'Probably dirt.' He is satisfied.
Outpost cook: 'Stew of the day is stew. Ask no questions, get no answers.'
Foreman: 'Fuel is cheap. Orange sky is free. Please stay off the gantries.'
Clerk: 'The Gate direct saves 114 Mk and skips Oort. The Heliopause is harder that way.'
Refiner: 'Smells like a campfire made of rubber. You'll stop noticing by Friday.'
Overheard: 'The Gate jump takes no time at all. The wait for it takes plenty.'
Dockhand: 'Buy rations here for the long stretch. Oort Beacon is thin on supplies.'
Trader: 'Titan methane in jugs. Good for lamps, bad for matches.'
Mechanic: 'Last drive checkup before the Gate. Don't skip it. The Gate skips nothing.'
A widow in a rubber coat sells pies. 'Methane-baked,' she says. 'Safe. Mostly.'
Lane clerk: 'The Kuiper Gate is a legal border. Bring a pen. And some patience.'
Overheard: 'My brother says space dysentery is a rumor. My brother is in the infirmary.'
A boy plays catch with a bolt. 'Gravity is low here,' says his dad. 'Aim is not.'
Foreman: 'Flare season up ahead. Rest here, repair here, regret nothing here.'
Beacon keeper: 'Last light before the Proxima shell. Please keep your running lights on.'
Dockhand: 'Rations here cost three times Ceres. Don't blame me. Blame the distance.'
Overheard: 'The Heliopause Shock is next. It is called a shock for a reason.'
Lane clerk: 'Please sign the guest log. We like to know who might not return.'
A hermit tends the beacon lamp. 'Eleven years,' he says. 'Good company, the dark.'
Mechanic: 'Check your hull seals. The Shock rattles loose bolts and loose resolve.'
Trader: 'Nothing here is cheap. Nothing here is rotten, either. Barely.'
Overheard: 'I counted my rations. Then I counted them again. The Beacon makes you count.'
Beacon keeper: 'Forty ships logged this year. Thirty-one made the other side.'
A child waves at the dark outside. 'Hello, Proxima,' she says. Nobody corrects her.
Dockhand: 'Flare season has begun. Hug the hull of whatever is bigger than you.'
Clerk: 'Customs on the far side may ask about your cargo. Answer slowly.'
Clerk: 'Final station before New Willamette. Final prices, too. Do not hope.'
Dockhand: 'The Flare Belt is in season. Hire a tug if you can. If you can't, ride low.'
Overheard: 'Two hundred Mk past the Belt and you're home. Home is mud, I hear.'
Trader: 'Nobody haggles at the end of the road. They pay and hold the receipt.'
Lane clerk: 'Arrivals are logged by rank. Pathfinder, Spacer, Groundling. We do not make the ranks.'
Mechanic: 'Fix everything you can fix. The Belt does the rest.'
A veteran settler: 'I made it in '81. The mud is real. The tomatoes are worth it.'
Dockhand: 'Rest if you must. The flares will wait. They always do.'
A mother counts her children out loud. Five. 'Good,' she tells the stars.
Overheard: 'The last leg is the longest. It's only 201 Mk. Don't ask me why.'
Clerk: 'Please review the beacons on the wall. They are not decor.'
Priest: 'We say a short prayer for the Belt. It is a very short prayer. We are optimistic.'
